types.name: Fenrir::CaretRect
types.doc: A rectangle in a window's logical coordinates, from its top-left corner (the mouse's units).

types.name: Fenrir::WindowId
types.doc: Which window an input came from. A plain number chosen by whoever feeds the input (FenrirWindow, which keys its windows by it, or a test); FenrirInput only compares it.

types.name: Fenrir::WindowInputClaims
types.doc: What a router is doing with input in one window (its input claims), or, in InputClaims, the union of every router's. Claims describe the interaction; they never filter events.

fields.name: pointer
fields.doc: The pointer is over the router's UI.

fields.name: pointerCapture
fields.doc: The router has captured the pointer (a drag that began on its UI): the window's pointer events go to it first. Raising it cancels the game's held mouse buttons in the window.

fields.name: keyboardFocus
fields.doc: The router has keyboard focus. Raising it cancels the game's held keys in the window.

fields.name: textInput
fields.doc: The router wants text: FenrirWindow keeps the window's text input on, with the caret below.

fields.name: caret
fields.doc: Where text is being typed, for the IME: read only with `textInput`.

types.name: Fenrir::Detail::ScriptWindowClaims
types.doc: One window's claims in InputClaims: which window, and what the routers claim in it.

types.name: Fenrir::Detail::ScriptInputClaims
types.doc:
The union of the input claims every input router publishes (ADR-0027), FenrirInput's InputClaims app resource as C# reads it: per window, each claim is raised if any router raises it, and the caret is that of the highest-priority router claiming text input; the gamepad claim is app-wide. Routers stay C++, so scripts read the claims and never publish them.

The view is of the claims as they were when it was got: get it again in a later system to see newer ones. It holds up to MaxWindows windows; claims in more windows than that are left out, with a warning in a debug build. With no input installed in the app there is none. InputClaims keeps its windows in a vector, which C# cannot read in place, so FenrirInputScripting keeps this plain-data copy as an app resource of its own and refreshes it from InputClaims whenever C# gets it.
